parts.title: 7-Day Topic Progression Outline
parts.body:
## 7-Day Linear Algebra Study Schedule — Day-by-Day Topic Outline

| Day | Primary Topic | Secondary / Reinforcement Topic | Suggested Practice Focus |
|-----|---------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **1** | Vector notation, geometric interpretation (R², R³), and vector arithmetic (addition, scalar multiplication, negation) | Building intuition for vector spaces as sets closed under addition and scalar multiplication | Compute 15 vector sums/differences and scalar multiples; sketch each result geometrically; verify commutativity and associativity with numeric examples |
| **2** | Dot product, cross product (R³), and linear combinations of vectors | Linear independence, span, and the geometric meaning of dependent vs. independent sets | Calculate dot and cross products for 10 vector pairs; for 6 given sets of 2–3 vectors, test linear independence via the cross/dot-product criteria and state the span geometrically |
| **3** | Matrix multiplication, matrix properties (distributivity, associativity, non-commutativity), and the transpose operation | Viewing matrix–vector multiplication as a linear transformation (column interpretation vs. row interpretation) | Multiply matrices of sizes 2×3·3×2, 3×3·3×1, 1×4·4×1; verify (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ; map a simple 2×2 matrix acting on (1,0) and (0,1) to describe the transformation |
| **4** | Inverse matrices (2×2 formula, 3×3 cofactor/adjugate method), determinant, and rank | Cramer's rule intuition; when an inverse exists (det ≠ 0) and what rank tells you about column/row space | Compute inverses and determinants for five 2×2 and three 3×3 matrices; find the rank of four sample matrices; solve two small Ax = b systems using A⁻¹ and verify by substitution |
| **5** | Gaussian elimination, row-echelon / reduced-echelon form, and consistency (unique, infinite, or no solution) | Homogeneous vs. non-homogeneous systems; expressing the solution set in parametric form | Perform full Gaussian elimination on four systems (3×3 and 4×4); classify each as consistent/inconsistent and unique/infinite; write the general solution with free variables |
| **6** | Mixed timed problem set spanning vectors, matrices, and systems (the "big-picture" integration day) | Connecting the threads: how a system's coefficient matrix encodes the vector relationships, and how rank/inverse/elimination are three lenses on the same question | 30-minute timed set: 5 vector-problem items, 5 matrix-operation items, 5 system-solve items; afterwards, annotate each problem with which Day 1–5 concept it tests and flag any that took > 3 min |
| **7** | Full review of all key definitions and theorems; targeted re-drill of weak spots identified on Day 6 | Self-assessment quiz and readiness gap-analysis for numerical linear algebra (what must be solid before pivoting to SVD, QR, iterative solvers, etc.) | 20-question self-test (multiple-choice + short-answer) covering every topic from Days 1–5; review every mistake in detail; write a one-page personal summary of the ten core concepts and note any lingering uncertainties |

### Progression Logic

- **Days 1 → 2:** Build the vector toolbox (arithmetic → inner products → combinations/independence) so that the language of "column space" and "null space" has meaning when matrices appear.
- **Days 3 → 4:** Introduce matrices as operators, then equip the student with the three diagnostic tools (inverse, determinant, rank) that will be reused in every system-solving step.
- **Day 5:** Unify vectors + matrices into the central algorithm of elementary linear algebra — Gaussian elimination — and make the consistency/solution-set vocabulary concrete.
- **Day 6:** Force integration; mixed problems prevent the "silo effect" where a student can do dot products in isolation but cannot set up and solve a 3×3 system from a word problem.
- **Day 7:** Consolidate and self-diagnose, producing the readiness signal for moving on to numerical linear algebra.

## 7-Day Linear Algebra Study Schedule

| Day | Primary Topic | Sub-topics Covered | Practice/Exercise Focus | Suggested Study Time |
|-----|---------------|--------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| **1** | **Vectors – Foundations** | Vector notation (column/row); geometric interpretation in ℝ² and ℝ³; vector addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, negation; commutativity & associativity of vector arithmetic; intuition for vector spaces as closed sets | Compute 15 vector sums/differences and scalar multiples; sketch each result on a coordinate plane; verify commutativity and associativity with numeric examples; write a 3-sentence verbal description of what "span" means geometrically | 2.5 – 3 hrs |
| **2** | **Vectors – Products & Independence** | Dot product (algebraic & geometric definitions); cross product in ℝ³; linear combinations; linear dependence vs. independence; span of a set of vectors; orthogonal vs. parallel vectors | Calculate dot and cross products for 10 vector pairs; for 6 given sets of 2–3 vectors, test linear independence using the cross/dot-product criteria and state the span geometrically; identify 4 pairs as orthogonal, parallel, or neither | 2.5 – 3 hrs |
| **3** | **Matrices – Operations & Transformations** | Matrix multiplication (dimensional compatibility rule); distributivity, associativity, non-commutativity; transpose operation; matrix–vector product as a linear transformation; column vs. row interpretation of the transformation | Multiply matrices of sizes 2×3·3×2, 3×3·3×1, 1×4×4×1; verify (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ with 3 random pairs; apply a simple 2×2 matrix to (1,0) and (0,1) and describe the resulting geometric transformation (stretch, rotation, shear) | 3 – 3.5 hrs |
| **4** | **Matrices – Inverse, Determinant & Rank** | 2×2 inverse formula; 3×3 inverse via cofactor/adjugate method; determinant (cofactor expansion, properties); rank of a matrix; invertibility criterion (det ≠ 0); Cramer's rule intuition; column space vs. null space | Compute inverses and determinants for five 2×2 and three 3×3 matrices; find the rank of four sample matrices; solve two small Ax = b systems using A⁻¹ and verify by direct substitution; for each matrix, state dim(col-space) and dim(null-space) | 3 – 3.5 hrs |
| **5** | **Systems of Equations – Gaussian Elimination** | Gaussian elimination algorithm; row-echelon form (REF) and reduced-echelon form (RREF); pivot positions and free variables; consistency classification (unique / infinite / no solution); homogeneous vs. non-homogeneous systems; parametric form of the solution set | Perform full Gaussian elimination on four systems (two 3×3, two 4×4); classify each as consistent/inconsistent and unique/infinite; write the general solution with free variables in parametric vector form; identify one system whose coefficient matrix is singular and explain why in terms of rank | 3 – 3.5 hrs |
| **6** | **Integrated Practice Day (Vectors + Matrices + Systems)** | Cross-topic synthesis: how a system's coefficient matrix encodes vector relationships; how rank, inverse, and elimination are three lenses on the same question; translating word problems into matrix equations; common pitfalls across all three pillars | 30-minute timed mixed set: 5 vector items, 5 matrix-operation items, 5 system-solve items; afterwards, annotate each problem with which Day 1–5 concept it tests; flag any item that took > 3 minutes and redo it the next morning; write a 5-bullet "what surprised me" reflection | 3 – 3.5 hrs |
| **7** | **Full Review & Self-Assessment** | Re-drill of every key definition and theorem from Days 1–5; targeted re-solve of weak spots identified on Day 6; self-assessment quiz; readiness gap-analysis for numerical linear algebra (SVD, QR, iterative solvers) | 20-question self-test (multiple-choice + short-answer) covering all topics from Days 1–5; review every mistake in detail and write the correct solution; compose a one-page personal summary listing the ten core concepts and note any lingering uncertainties; set 2 concrete goals for the next study block | 3 – 4 hrs |

### Coverage Checklist

- **Vectors** → Days 1, 2 (dedicated) + reinforced in Days 3, 5, 6
- **Matrices** → Days 3, 4 (dedicated) + reinforced in Days 5, 6
- **Systems of Equations** → Day 5 (dedicated) + reinforced in Days 4, 6
- **Dedicated Practice / Review** → Day 6 (mixed timed practice) and Day 7 (full review & self-assessment)

### How to Use This Table

1. **Read** the Primary Topic and Sub-topics before starting to frame your session.
2. **Work through** the Practice/Exercise Focus items by hand (pen & paper); avoid passive re-reading.
3. **Respect the time block.** If a topic runs long, trim sub-topics rather than skipping the practice column.
4. **End each day** by writing 2–3 sentences in a study journal summarising what you could do and what still feels shaky—this feeds directly into Day 7's gap-analysis.

parts.title: 10-Concept Readiness Checklist
parts.body:
## Readiness Checklist: 10 Concepts Before Numerical Linear Algebra

*If you can check off all ten items below with confidence, you are prepared to move on to numerical linear algebra (SVD, QR factorisation, iterative solvers, condition numbers, etc.).*

- [ ] **1. Vector Operations** – Can compute addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, dot product, and cross product for vectors in ℝ² and ℝ³, and sketch or verbally interpret each result (direction, magnitude, orthogonality) on a coordinate diagram.

- [ ] **2. Linear Independence / Dependence** – Given a set of 2–4 vectors in ℝ³, can determine whether they are linearly independent or dependent (via cross-product / dot-product criteria or row-reduction) and state the span geometrically (a line, a plane, or all of ℝ³).

- [ ] **3. Matrix Multiplication & Properties** – Can multiply matrices of compatible dimensions (e.g., 2×3 · 3×2) by hand without error, verify associativity, distributivity, and the transpose rule (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ, and demonstrate with a concrete counter-example that multiplication is not commutative.

- [ ] **4. Inverse Matrix** – Can compute the inverse of a 2×2 matrix using the shortcut formula and of a 3×3 matrix via the adjugate/cofactor method, and verify correctness by confirming A·A⁻¹ = I; can also state when an inverse does not exist.

- [ ] **5. Determinant** – Can compute the determinant of a 2×2 and 3×3 matrix using cofactor expansion, interpret det(A) geometrically as a signed volume scale factor, and explain what det(A) = 0 implies (volume collapse, linearly dependent columns, non-invertibility).

- [ ] **6. Rank & Nullity** – Can row-reduce a 4×5 matrix to find its rank, compute the nullity as dim(null(A)), and verify the Rank–Nullity Theorem (rank + nullity = number of columns); can state the dimension of the column space and null space for any given matrix.

- [ ] **7. Gaussian Elimination** – Can carry out full Gaussian elimination on a 4×4 augmented matrix [A | b] to reach both REF and RREF, correctly identify pivot positions and free variables, and write the general solution set in parametric vector form (x = x_p + t·v + s·w …).

- [ ] **8. Consistency of Systems** – Given the augmented matrix [A | b], can classify the system as *consistent-unique*, *consistent-infinite*, or *inconsistent* and justify the classification by comparing rank(A) with rank([A | b]); can recognise a singular-coefficient system and explain why it has no unique solution.

- [ ] **9. Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors (Intro)** – Can set up and solve the characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0 for a 2×2 (and a simple 3×3) matrix to obtain all eigenvalues, and for each eigenvalue can find the eigenspace (kernel of A − λI) and write a basis of eigenvectors.

- [ ] **10. Geometric Interpretation – Column & Row Spaces** – Can describe the column space of a matrix as the span of its column vectors and the row space as the span of its row vectors, relate both to the geometry of the linear map x ↦ Ax (domain restriction to row space, codomain image = column space), and connect these subspaces to the solutions of Ax = b and Ax = 0.

---

**How to use this checklist:** Work through each item as a *self-test*—attempt a concrete problem of the described type without notes. If any item feels shaky, revisit the corresponding day(s) in the 7-day schedule and redo the associated practice exercises before advancing to numerical linear algebra.
